newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Saab's Hendry says firm developing as planned.
newsitem.headline: Saab's Hendry says firm developing as planned.

text.p: Swedish vehicle maker Saab Automobile AB said on Thursday the company was developing according to plan but would not post a profit for 1996.
Saab Automobile managing director Robert Hendry, speaking to the American Chamber of Commerce in Stockholm, repeated that he was expecting the company to swing to profit within 18 months.
But he added: "Often things get worse before they get better." Saab is jointly owned by U.S. General Motors Corp and Swedish investment company Investor AB.
"This year we have had a stronger crown and higher production costs. But we are developing according to the plans I have for the company," he said.
This year increased production costs were behind a fall in Saab Auto's profit, but in 1997 marketing and development costs will hit profits, he said.
Saab planned to win back lost market share in Sweden by next year with the help of new company car regulations in Sweden that ease the tax burden on corporate car drivers.

In 1995 Saab posted a profit of 148 million crowns before tax mainly because of a fourth quarter profit of 275 million crowns. The company will not be publishing results for the first nine months of 1996.
